doc.title: Bernard Purdie interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003

title: Identifying To Be Free versions on playback
summary: Rowe plays a tune and Purdie identifies it as To Be Free, which he played on in four hit versions, including Nina Simone in 1964.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Good. Well I was going to play, actually, a tune that you played on, and I want to see if you can remember what it is.
Well it sounds like the original was done by Little Esther. I did the original. Little Esther Phillips. “To Be Free.” Nina Simone — I did the first one with Nina in ’64.
This is actually Shirley Scott I think.
I know. I was coming to it. But I’m just trying to tell you—
Or you’re giving me the whole — that’s great.
So it’s funny with you, it’s not just that you played on that one, you played on all four versions of it. That’s terrific.

Yeah. But see that’s what happens. Now I can’t tell you why all the other things just came up. And I can just say it because it happened. That’s what I mean by what’s in the memory bank. When you hear something. Something strikes up and then all of a sudden you go back to what you did originally. And I find that yeah, there are four different versions that I did that were all hits by the different people. And then you pick out one that wasn’t necessarily a big hit for her but yet yeah, it was me also. And that’s a nice feeling for me, that people are finding those kind of records. And that’s what he’s been doing. He’s been finding records that do have some information on them.

Exactly. But there was people in recording studios who now have been putting down documentation of what — all these other books and stuff that’s been written by different people, the documentations of interviews of other people who’ve been talking about me for umpteen years. And there is it. So it’s a really, really nice feeling for me to find that these kind of things have been happening. And boy I’m telling you, my book is dynamite. I really like what he is doing. Even with the bad stuff, it’s good. I’m tickled pink. I’m serious. I’m tickled pink about it. It’s another ballgame for me.
